review_scope.structural_evidence: Four draft articles; exact question revisions; only existing tags; two displayed links each; whitespace word counts 193, 202, 199, 197.
review_scope.method: Blind-solved candidate questions before reading sources.json or articles.json, then opened and checked every displayed source URL and the frozen full bodies.

checked_claims: AFI credits Audrey Hepburn as Holly Golightly and identifies the Capote 1958 novella adaptation.
AFI reports Marilyn Monroe as a contender during casting, correctly kept distinct from the final credit.
The Academy page records five nominations, two wins for Mancini's score and Moon River, and Hepburn as an Actress nominee rather than winner.
items.distractor_review: Marilyn Monroe and Shirley MacLaine were candidates in the casting history, and Natalie Wood was not Holly. None is a defensible finished-film answer; the wording asks who played the role.

checked_claims: AFI credits Robert De Niro as Travis Bickle and Paul Schrader and Martin Scorsese in their stated writing and directing roles.
AFI supports the taxi-driving preparation and attributes the mirror-scene improvisation account to Scorsese.
The Academy page identifies the 1977 ceremony as honoring 1976 releases and lists Taxi Driver nominations for film, Foster, and Herrmann; the body does not call them wins.
items.distractor_review: Jodie Foster, Harvey Keitel, and Albert Brooks are cast members in different roles. Robert De Niro is the sole actor playing Travis Bickle.

checked_claims: AFI credits Bette Davis as Margo Channing and Anne Baxter as Eve Harrington.
AFI states that Addison DeWitt, Karen Richards, and Margo Channing intermittently provide voice-over narration.
AFI identifies Mary Orr's The Wisdom of Eve in Hearst's International-Cosmopolitan (May 1946); the Academy page records the cited Best Motion Picture, Directing, and black-and-white costume wins.
items.distractor_review: Anne Baxter played Eve Harrington; Gloria Swanson and Joan Crawford do not play Margo Channing. Bette Davis is the unique answer.

checked_claims: AFI credits Marlon Brando as Terry Malloy, a former boxer and longshoreman, and credits Kazan and Schulberg as stated.
AFI supports the Malcolm Johnson 1948 New York Sun series, Schulberg's waterfront research, and the qualification that the film remains fictional drama.
The Academy event page supports shooting on both sides of the Hudson, 12 nominations, eight wins, and the Brando and Kazan wins.
items.distractor_review: Karl Malden played Father Barry, Rod Steiger played Charley Malloy, and Lee J. Cobb played Johnny Friendly. Only Marlon Brando played Terry Malloy.

release_boundary: Every verdict is accepted_for_draft through independent native source review only. This report does not state or imply external-provider approval, export, release, or publication.
